issues.body: main invokes run_gate_once before save_state_file. Verdict paths inside evaluate_once/render_verdict emit the summary and diagnostics before run_gate_once returns; only afterward does main persist terminal_exit. A crash, eviction, or save failure after publication leaves the previous nonterminal carrier, so a retry may fetch a changed sibling set and publish the opposite verdict. The replay tests always persist successfully, and the atomic-save failure test demonstrates that a failed replacement intentionally preserves the old record, so neither test covers this ambiguous-publication interval.
issues.fix_hint: Separate decision computation from authoritative publication. Persist the state containing terminal_exit atomically before rendering/publishing that persisted decision, then replay the committed decision for output. Add a CLI/transport-path test that forces the terminal-state save to fail and retries against the opposite sibling set, proving that no opposite verdict can be published. If Phase 1 intentionally cannot provide this guarantee, remove claims that ambiguous transport retries are closed and document it explicitly as a Phase-2 obligation.
issues.title: Verdict is still published before its terminal state is durably committed

verdict.summary: Round 4's major finding remains materially unchanged. main still calls run_gate_once first, allowing evaluate_once/render_verdict to publish the authoritative summary and diagnostics, and only afterward calls save_state_file. terminal_exit therefore protects duplicates only after that post-publication write succeeds. If the process is evicted or persistence fails in the interval, the old nonterminal carrier remains; a retry can observe a changed sibling set and publish the opposite verdict. The new replay tests cover successfully persisted terminal records, while the atomic-save test confirms failed writes preserve the previous record rather than closing this publication/commit gap. Progress is stagnant.
